records.name: Lida
records.facts_used: The catalogue explains Lida through Lidija: Greek Lydia «Lydian woman, inhabitant of Lydia», a region of Asia Minor. These are the source words used in the explanation; they describe the name’s formation, not a trait shared by everyone bearing it. The Siliņš catalogue records a historical detail for this exact form: 1884; calendar 1889 (dictionary page 214). This dates an attributed record of use and calendar inclusion. It does not mean that the name was created then, and the separate dates for Lidija are not transferred to Lida.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Checked location: Siliņš catalogue (izpetnieks.lv, cached LV-SILINS-LIDA-R83), dictionary p. 214. The 1884 record carries the catalogue source abbreviation “Lkp”, not expanded or independently inspected; it is not called the first use. Lidija’s separate 1881 Rūjiena / 1899 calendar dates were not transferred.

records.name: Gordejs
records.facts_used: The Latvian name-rendering manual gives the exact Russian correspondence Гордей → Gordejs. This is a documented spelling relationship between a source-language personal name and its Latvian adaptation; the older Siliņš dictionary has no entry for this exact form, so no meaning is asserted here. The exact row appears in the 1993 manual on printed page 197. This dates the published rendering recommendation. It does not identify the first Latvian birth registration, and explanations given for other names beginning Gord- are not transferred to this form.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Visually checked LV-LVA-RU93 PDF p. 90 / printed p. 197, row Гордей → Gordejs (patronymic Гордеевич; Latvian genitive Gordeja). records.name: Marcelis
records.facts_used: The Senn–Salys dictionary gives Marcelis as a personal name corresponding to Latin Marcellus and also as a short form of Marcelinas and Marcelijonas. Behind the Name explains Marcellus as a Roman cognomen, originally a diminutive of Marcus, borne by two popes. Salys’s Lithuanian calendar for 1964, reprinted in 1983, prints Marcelis (Marcys) on 16 January, the same day as the present calendar. This is a dated calendar use of the exact name and its short form; it does not identify the first Lithuanian bearer.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Visually checked LT-SALYS83 PDF p. 249 / printed p. 234 (Marcėlis, accented headword; 1. PN Marcellus, 2. KF of Marcelinas and Marcelijonas; Marcis (dial.) = Marcėlis) and PDF p. 301 / printed p. 286 (16 January: Marcelis (Marcys)). INT-BTN Marcellus cached as INT-BTN-MARCELLUS. Calendar date coincides with the project calendar.

records.name: Ilmo
records.facts_used: Julius Mägiste lists Ilmo as a Finnish name taken from the University of Helsinki almanac for 1929, and compares it with the Estonian word ilm, “weather; world”. The comparison is his; it does not give the name a fixed literal meaning. His collection of Estonian-style personal names was published in Tartu in 1929 (printed page 28). This dates a published recommendation and a documented Finnish source; it does not identify the first Estonian child named Ilmo.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Visually checked EE-MAGISTE29-AES PDF p. 34 / printed p. 28: “Ilmo (sm. Alm., vrd. ilm -a)”; abbreviation key PDF p. 15: Alm. = Almanakka vuodeksi 1929, Helsingin Yliopisto; sm. = Finnish. EE-RAJANDI66 PDF 202 / printed 204 supplementary list has “Ilmo 35/40”, but the source abbreviation 35/40 was not resolved, so no dated birth record is claimed.
